2) Snelcontrole met uw boekhouder (eigen: 2) Quick check with your bookkeeper (owner: entrepreneur + bookkeeper) - Question: which import options exist now? (automatic bank feed, CSV import, API integration, plug-in) - Question: which fields do we need to automatically match transactions? (amount, date, ref/description, payment reference) - End result: choice of the simplest short-term route (e.g. daily CSV import) and long-term option (API/webhook).
3) Kies de implementatiestrategie (eigen: 3) Choose the implementation strategy (owner: financial manager or IT manager) - Option A — short term: automated exports/imports - Set up a daily bank export or automatic CSV import. Good if development capacity is limited. - Metric: reduction in manual processing (e.g. hours/week less) and the percentage of transactions matched without manual intervention. - Option B — medium/long term: API or webhook integration - If both parties support APIs (and authentication like OAuth 2.0 is possible), have a developer or integrator build a secure connection. - Metric: % automatic matching, time between payment and booking (set your own target).
Beperkingen en risico’s - Technisch: nie: Limitations and risks - Technical: not every payment provider offers the same data quality or real-time webhooks. You cannot always match everything automatically. - Privacy and security: API connections require good security and clear consent; work together with your accountant and technical lead. - Evidence limitation: the presence of OAuth 2.0 in an accounting package only proves that secure authorization is possible; it does not guarantee an out-of-the-box connection with your specific payment provider.
